Below is a cohesive 12-week plan summary that integrates: cardio with safe progression for weight loss, a strengthened emphasis on resistance training including compound lifts (squats and deadlifts) with safe progressions, a tested approach to a future 5K readiness, and a cardiac-health–mocused nutrition plan. It’s tailored for a 58-year-old man, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity work, with a full gym.

How to read this plan
- Phase structure: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3), Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6), Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9), Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12).
- Weekly template: 4 training days per week (2 cardio days + 2 resistance days), optional mobility/active recovery day.
- Intensity cues: HR targets ~95–115 bpm for steady cardio; RPE 4–6/10 for most cardio; resistance sets are 8–12 reps with light-to-moderate loads; no max lifts; no if signs of chest pain, dizziness, severe SOB.
- Progression: small, conservative increases every 1–3 weeks, controlled by form, HR, and RPE.

Phase 1: Foundation and habit formation with initial strength (Weeks 1–3)
Goals:
- Establish routine, technique, and safety.
- Build aerobic base and introduce light resistance with compound exposure.
- Begin 5–10 minutes core/mobility daily.

Weekly structure
- Day 1: Cardio + Core
  - Cardio: 20–25 minutes steady-state at moderate pace; HR ~95–105 bpm; RPE 4–5/10.
  - Core/mobility: 6–12 minutes (Dead Bug 2x8–12 per side, Bird-Dog 2x10 per side, Pallof press 2x8–10 per side, Cat-Cow 2–3 minutes).
- Day 2: Resistance Day 1 (Full body; emphasis on technique, light loads)
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio
  - Goblet squat: 3x12 (tempo 2–0–2–0)
  - Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: 3x12
  - Chest press (machine or dumbbells): 3x12
  - Seated row (machine/cable): 3x12
  - Lat pulldown: 2–3x12
  - Shoulder press (light): 2–3x12
  - Leg curl: 2x12
  - Core: Pallof press 2x10 per side; Modified plank 2x20–25s
- Day 3: Rest or Mobility
- Day 4: Cardio Intervals (short, controlled)
  - 6–8 cycles: 45 seconds brisk effort, 75–90 seconds easy; total 16–20 minutes plus warm-up/cool-down
- Day 5: Optional Light Resistance Day or Mobility
  - Optional light circuit: 2 sets of 10–12 per exercise with light loads, focus on breathing and technique
- Day 6–7: Rest or gentle activity

Progression cues (Weeks 2–3)
- If 12 reps completed with good form, add 2–5% weight on 1–2 exercises or add 1–2 reps on all sets.
- Cardio: add 5 minutes to one day if HR and RPE allow.

Phase 2: Strength endurance with greater volume and compound emphasis (Weeks 4–6)
Goals:
- Increase total weekly resistance volume; incorporate more compounds with controlled ROM.
- Expand cardio variety and cumulative time to support fat loss.

Weekly structure
- Cardio: 3 days/week
  - Day A: 35–40 minutes steady-state; HR 95–112 bpm
  - Day B: Intervals: 8 cycles of 60 seconds moderate-to-brisk with 1:30–2:00 easy; total ~16–22 minutes
  - Day D: 40–45 minutes easy-to-moderate
- Resistance: 4 days/week (upper/lower split to increase volume)
  - Lower body: Goblet squat or barbell squat (light); 3x10–12
  - Dumbbell RDL or trap-bar deadlift (light): 3x10–12
  - Leg extensions/leg curls: 2x12
  - Upper body push: Chest press or incline press: 3x10–12
  - Upper body pull: Seated row or cable row: 3x10–12
  - Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
  - Shoulder press: 2–3x10–12
  - Accessory: Face pulls 2x12; Pallof press 3x8–10 per side
  - Core: 3 rounds 8–12 reps
- Progression cues:
  - If 12 reps with control, increase weight 2–5% or add 1–2 reps.
  - Maintain tempo 2–0–2–0 to ensure control.

Phase 3: Functional strength endurance and higher work capacity (Weeks 7–9)
Goals:
- Build muscular endurance, maintain aerobic base, and emphasize functional movement patterns (unilateral work, compound lifts with safe form).

Weekly structure
- Cardio: 3 days/week
  - Day A: 40 minutes steady-state; HR 95–110 bpm
  - Day B: Intervals: 8–10 cycles of 60 seconds hard with 90 seconds easy
  - Day D: 45 minutes steady-state with optional short bursts
- Resistance: 4 days/week (structured as four-day push/pull/legs-ish with a full-body integration day)
  - Lower body: Front squat or goblet squat 3x10–12 (progress to 3x8–10 with light barbell if form is solid)
  - Hip hinge: Dumbbell RDL or barbell RDL 3x10–12
  - Split squats or Bulgarian split squats: 2–3x10–12 per leg
  - Upper body push: Incline press or dumbbell bench press 3x10–12
  - Upper body pull: Seated row or cable row 3x10–12
  - Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
  - Shoulder press: 3x10–12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x8–10 per side; side planks 2x15–20s
- Progression cues:
  - If form is solid, add 2–5% weight or 1–2 reps every 2–3 weeks.
  - Consider a tempo emphasis for some sets (2–0–2–0) to boost time under tension.

Phase 4: Conditioning, consolidation, and final adaptations (Weeks 10–12)
Goals:
- Solidify routine, sustain gains, and prepare for the 5K readiness plan and ongoing maintenance.

Weekly structure
- Cardio: 3–4 days/week
  - Day A: 40–45 minutes steady-state; HR 95–112 bpm
  - Day B: Interval day: 8 cycles of 1 minute hard with 1 minute easy (or 6 cycles of 90 seconds hard with 2 minutes easy), total 20–30 minutes
  - Day D: 30–40 minutes easy plus optional short interval block (20–30 seconds) if tolerated
  - Weekend: optional longer easy session (60 minutes) if energy allows
- Resistance: 4 days/week
  - Lower body: Goblet squat or barbell back squat (light) 3x10–12
  - Hip hinge: Romanian deadlift 3x10–12
  - Leg extensions/curls: 2x12
  - Upper body push: Chest press or incline press 3x10–12
  - Upper body pull: Seated row or lat pulldown 3x10–12
  - Shoulders: Overhead press 3x10–12
  - Core: 3 rounds of 12–15 reps (anti-rotation, dead bug) or a 60–90s bridge hold
- Optional: One light density circuit day per week to boost metabolic conditioning without high fatigue

5K readiness and testing blocks (embedded safety-focused progression)
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Begin run-walk development for 5K readiness as a cardio progression on Day A or Day D. Use walk/run intervals (e.g., 1–2 minutes run, 1–2 minutes walk) for 20–25 minutes total, progressing to longer running blocks.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Seed the 5K readiness test:
  - Week 11: Run-walk progression culminating in 25–30 minutes continuous run-walk or a controlled 5K distance with walk breaks as needed.
  - Week 12: Optional submax 5K time trial if clinician approves and symptoms are stable; otherwise, perform a non-competitive 5K distance with walk breaks to assess tolerance and pace.

Nutrition plan (cardiac-health focus; aligned to training)
- Daily protein: 1.4–1.6 g/kg/day to preserve lean mass during weight loss and training.
- Calories: Modest deficit to support weight loss (250–500 kcal/day below maintenance), adjusted by weekly weight changes and clinician guidance.
- Carbs: Consume around workouts (1–2 hours pre, 1–2 hours post) to support energy and recovery.
- Fat: 25–35% of daily calories, emphasizing unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, avocado, fatty fish).
- Fiber: 25–38 g/day; aim for at least 2–3 servings of vegetables at lunch/dinner and a fruit daily.
- Sodium: 1,500–2,300 mg/day target, per clinician guidance.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 liters/day, more on training days.
- Alcohol: Up to 1 drink/day for men; discuss with clinician given post-MI status.
- Meal pattern: 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks; pre-workout snack 30–60 minutes before training; post-workout meal within 1–2 hours after training.

Safety and monitoring
- Heart rate and exertion: Regression to HR- or RPE-based guidance after medications; watch for chest pain, dizziness, excessive SOB.
- Valsalva avoidance: Exhale during exertion; maintain stable core stabilization.
- Max lifts: No max lifts; focus on technique and control.
- Recovery: Prioritize sleep (7–9 hours), hydration, and nutrition to support recovery.

Tracking and progression
- Use a simple weekly log: HR (if suitable), RPE, load, reps, distance/time for cardio, and any symptoms.
- Reassess every 4 weeks with objective measures: ability to perform more reps/weight, improved HR tolerance, longer cardio duration at target HR, and readiness for the 5K test.
- Coordinate with clinician for any new symptoms or medication changes.

Equipment and customization notes
- If available equipment differs (barbells, trap bars, machines), I can tailor the exact compound lifts and progression to your gym setup.
- For shoulder health and shoulder stability, substitute or constrain pressing movements as needed.
- If you want a printable, week-by-week calendar with specific daily workouts (including exact sets, reps, rest times, and progression milestones), I can generate that.

Would you like me to produce a detailed, printable 12-week calendar that includes:
- Week-by-week daily workouts (Day A, Day B, Day D, Day E) with precise exercises, sets, reps, tempo, rest, and cardio HR/RPE targets
- A separate 5K readiness progression with run/walk targets for Weeks 7–12
- A complete nutrition checklist with weekly meal templates and portion estimates based on the client’s weight
- A printable grocery list and a 2-page safety/screening checklist for HIIT and the 5K test?

If you share the client’s current equipment (treadmill/bike availability), approximate body weight, and any cardiologist notes, I’ll tailor the plan precisely and format it for printing.

Below is a conservative, general-fitness 12-week program designed for a 58-year-old male, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity work with HR targets under ~115 bpm (approximately 70% of age-predicted max). Emphasis is on gradual progression, low-to-moderate intensity, no valsalva, no maximal lifts, and a full-gym approach covering cardio, resistance training, mobility, and recovery. Always ensure physician clearance and monitor RPE/HR; sessions should be stopped if chest pain, undue shortness of breath, dizziness, or new symptoms occur.

Program structure at a glance
- Frequency: 4 training days per week (2 cardio-focused days, 2 full-body resistance days). Optional 5th day for mobility/active recovery if tolerated.
- Phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3), Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6), Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9), Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12).
- Cardio intensity: Zone corresponding to moderate effort; keep HR ≈ 95–115 bpm (adjust per individual monitoring and RPE 4–6/10). Include warm-up and cool-down with 5–10 minutes each.
- Resistance: Submaximal loading, 2–3 sets per exercise, 10–15 reps per set initially, focusing on form and control. Prospective progression: add small weight or tempo adjustments every 2–3 weeks if tolerated, never approaching failure or heavy lifting.
- Flexibility and mobility: brief daily mobility and thoracic spine work; breathing and relaxation techniques integrated.

Weeks 1–3: Foundation and habituation (Phase 1)
Goals: Establish routine, emphasize technique, build basic aerobic base, introduce resistance with light loads.

Weekly schedule (example):
- Day A: Cardio + Core
  - Cardio: 20–25 minutes continuous at moderate pace on treadmill or cycle, RPE 4–5/10, HR ~95–105 bpm.
  - Core & mobility: 5–10 minutes
    - Dead Bug: 2 sets x 8–12 reps per side
    - Bird-Dog: 2x10 per side
    - Pallof press (standing, light resistance): 2x8–10 per side
    - Cat-Cow and thoracic mobility: 2–3 minutes
- Day B: Resistance Training (full body, machines first)
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio
  - Leg press or leg extension/clexion: 2x12–15
  - Seated leg curl: 2x12–15
  - Chest press (machine): 2x12–15
  - Seated row (machine or cable): 2x12–15
  - Lat pulldown (assisted if needed): 2x12–15
  - Shoulder press (machine, light): 2x12–15
  - Dumbbell deadlift or hip hinge with light dumbbells: 2x12–15
  - Core: carried out after resistance: Plank (modified) 2x15–20 seconds; Side plank 2x10–15 seconds per side
  - Cool-down: 5–10 minutes gentle stretch
- Day C: Rest or Mobility day (optional light/activity)
- Day D: Cardio Intervals (optionally after resistance on Day B)
  - Cardio intervals: 6–8 cycles of 1 minute at a brisk but sustainable pace (RPE 5–6/10) followed by 2 minutes easy, total 16–20 minutes, HR within target, cool-down
- Day E/F: Optional light cardio or mobility days as tolerated

Progression cues for Weeks 2–3:
- Increase cardio duration by 5 minutes if HR target maintained and RPE remains in 4–6/10.
- Resistance sets: stay at 2x12–15; if comfortable, introduce a light third set (e.g., one more set of one or two exercises) or increase weight by a small amount (e.g., 2–5%) only if form is perfect and HR remains controlled.

Key notes:
- Breath control: no Valsalva; exhale on exertion.
- Warm-up: include 5–10 minutes of light cardio plus dynamic mobility.
- Pain: stop if chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness; notify clinician if symptoms arise.

Weeks 4–6: Progressive loading and cardio variety (Phase 2)
Goals: Slightly higher cardio exposure, introduce more varied resistance exercises with lighter, controlled progression, and reinforce technique.

Weekly structure remains similar, with modifications:
- Cardio: 25–30 minutes steady-state 3 days/week, HR ~95–112 bpm; or add one longer cardio day of 35–40 minutes at easy-to-moderate pace.
- Resistance: 3 days/week (e.g., Tue/Thu/Sat)
  - Exercise selection shifts toward more free-weight and cable-based movements with controlled tempo.
  - Proposed sets/reps: 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps per exercise; target 60–70% 1RM estimate (use light loads, no max lifts).
  - Example Session:
    - Goblet squat or leg press: 2–3x10–12
    - Dumbbell bench press or chest press machine: 2–3x10–12
    - Seated row or cable row: 2–3x10–12
    - Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 2–3x10–12
    - Leg curl: 2–3x10–12
    - Cable or dumbbell Romanian deadlift (light): 2–3x10–12
    - Shoulder lateral raise (very light): 2–3x12–15
    - Core: as Week 1–3, add dead bug with resistance or pallof press 2x8–10
- Intensity and technique: prioritize form; avoid failure; RPE 5–6/10 during most sets.
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes post-workout.

Progression cues for Weeks 5–6:
- If 12 reps with good form achieved for all exercises in a session, consider adding a small increase in weight next session (2–5%), or add a light set (e.g., 3x10 instead of 2x10).
- Cardio progression: add 5 minutes to one session or introduce a longer 40-minute brisk walk/cycle at HR 95–110 bpm on one day.

Weeks 7–9: Moderate progression and functional emphasis (Phase 3)
Goals: Improve muscular endurance, maintain aerobic capacity, and introduce more functional movement patterns.

Weekly structure:
- Cardio: 3 days/week, 30–40 minutes total with mix of steady-state and light intervals.
  - Example:
    - Day 1: 30–35 min steady-state
    - Day 3: 20–25 min moderate intervals (1 min hard, 2 min easy)
    - Day 5: 40 min easy-to-moderate
  - HR targets: 95–115 bpm; ensure RPE 5–6/10
- Resistance: 3 days/week
  - Exercise selection: include variations that mimic daily activities; maintain 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps.
  - Sample session:
    - Leg press or squat pattern with lightweight goblet squats: 3x10–12
    - Dumbbell incline press or machine chest press: 3x10–12
    - Seated cable row or TRX row: 3x10–12
    - Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
    - Step-ups or reverse lunges (bodyweight or light dumbbells): 3x10–12 per leg
    - Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3x12
    - Shoulder press (machine or dumbbells, light): 3x10–12
    - Core: 3x10–12 including planks (progress duration slowly), side planks 2x15–20 seconds
- Tempo: consider slow/eccentric emphasis (2–0–2–0 cadence) for some exercises to improve control, but avoid breath-holding.

Progression cues:
- Weight increases only if all reps completed with proper form and HR remains in safe range.
- Consider 1–2 more reps per set or 2–5% more weight where feasible every 2 weeks.

Weeks 10–12: Consolidation and conditioning (Phase 4)
Goals: Consolidate gains, improve general conditioning, and reinforce sustainable healthy patterns.

Weekly structure:
- Cardio: 3–4 days/week, 30–45 minutes overall. Include one longer cardio session of 45 minutes easy-to-moderate pace if tolerated.
  - Optional: one day of gentle interval work (e.g., 1 minute at a brisk pace, 2 minutes easy, for 6–8 cycles) as tolerated and under HR cap.
- Resistance: 3 days/week
  - Emphasize form and consistency; continue 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps with modest progressive loading.
  - Exercise sample:
    - Barbell or dumbbell goblet squats (light to moderate): 3x10–12
    - Chest press or push-up variations (elevated if needed): 3x10–12
    - Seated row or cable row: 3x10–12
    - Lat pull-down or assisted pull-up: 3x10–12
    - Leg extension and leg curl: 3x12
    - Deadlift variation with light load or hip hinge (trap bar or DB): 2–3x10
    - Dumbbell shoulder press: 3x10–12
    - Core circuit: 3 rounds of 12–15 reps of anti-rotation or BRISK: Pallof press, cable anti-rotation, and dead bug
- Mobility and recovery: daily 5–15 minutes, plus 1–2 sessions of longer mobility work per week if possible.

General safety and programming notes
- Heart rate and exertion:
  - Target HR roughly 95–115 bpm for steady cardio; adjust for medications (beta-blockers) that blunt HR. Use RPE 4–6/10 for most sessions; avoid pushing to 7–9/10.

- Valsalva avoidance:
  - Instruct client to exhale during exertion, especially on lifting or standing up from exercise stations.
- Max lifts:
  - No attempts at near-max lifts. Use light-to-moderate loads where form is prioritized, especially early weeks.
- Breathing and technique cues:
  - Keep core engaged, neutral spine in all lifts, hips hinge with minimal knee collapse, and avoid twisting under load.
- Warm-up and cool-down:
  - Each session begins with 5–10 minutes of light cardio plus mobility; ends with 5–10 minutes of stretching and breathing work.
- Nutrition basics for rehab-friendly fitness:
  - Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day to support recovery and lean mass. Example: 84–112 g/day for a 70 kg person (adjust for client weight).
  - Hydration: 2–3 liters/day, more on training days.
  - Balanced meals: whole-food sources, including lean proteins, whole grains, healthy fats, and a variety of vegetables.
  - Consider a modest caloric intake maintenance or slight deficit only if weight management is a goal; consult with clinician if weight loss is desired.
  - Omega-3-rich foods (fatty fish, flaxseed) may help, but discuss with clinician if on medications.
- Recovery:
  - Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours.
  - Rest days: ensure at least 1 full rest day per week, with optional light activity or mobility work.
  - If experiencing soreness, reduce volume by 20–30% and slowly progress back.

Progress tracking and workload planning
- Use simple weekly logs: HR, RPE, and weight/load for each exercise; note any symptoms.
- Reassess every 4 weeks with objective measures: ability to complete more reps, more comfortable HR range, or increased distance in cardio.
- Communication with clinician: if any new symptoms or abnormal HR response occur, pause program and contact clinician.

Guidelines for adding HIIT safely
- Timing: introduce HIIT no earlier than Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9) if he has built a strong cardio base, good recovery, and strength tolerance. If any signs of instability (chest pain, undue fatigue, BP issues, abnormal HR response) appear, delay.
- Medical clearance: obtain explicit clearance from his cardiologist or rehab team for intervals and higher heart-rate targets. Confirm meds (e.g., beta-blockers) that blunt HR; rely on RPE and symptoms rather than HR.
- Modality and environment: use low-risk modalities (stationary bike or treadmill treadmill with rails, elliptical) in a supervised setting. Avoid maximal sprints; stay away from plyometrics or explosive lifts during HIIT blocks.
- Intensity prescription:
  - Work intervals: start with very short work bouts at low-to-moderate intensity, e.g., 15–20 seconds at RPE 6–7/10.
  - Recovery: 60–90 seconds easy pace or complete passive recovery.
  - Duration: begin with 4–6 cycles per session; total HIIT time 6–12 minutes, within a 20–30 minute cardio window including warm-up/cool-down.
  - Progression: every 2–3 weeks, add 1 more interval or extend work interval by 5–10 seconds if tolerance is excellent and HR/RPE remain safe.
- Monitoring:
  - Pre-session: verify resting HR, BP, symptom check.
  - During: watch for chest discomfort, undue breathlessness, dizziness, pale/clammy skin; stop if any arise.
  - Post: monitor recovery HR behavior and how long it takes to return to baseline.
- Protocol options (gradual ramp variants):
  - Bike HIIT example (Phase 3+):
    - 5-minute warm-up
    - 6 cycles: 20 seconds hard at RPE 6–7, 60–90 seconds easy
    - 5-minute cool-down
  - Treadmill incline-free or light incline version:

    - 6 cycles: 15–20 seconds at a brisk jog (if tolerated) or fast walk, 90 seconds easy
    - 5-minute cool-down
- Integration with resistance work:
